clue.text: Divisive 25 per cent cut in staff coming up

indicators.note: cut means a piece is chopped off the staff word, here at its end

parts.note: a staff is a pole, such as a flagpole
one letter of a four-letter word is a quarter of it, here the last letter
coming up is arising, emerging into view

explanation.surface: A staffing cut of a quarter is announced, and it splits the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming up' looks like a reversal signal but simply means arising, emerging.
explanation.definitionFit: Something polarising drives opinion to two opposed extremes, which is what a divisive issue does.

clue.text: Put flags on pavilion's front with welcoming word

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of pavilion
ave is a Latin greeting, hail

explanation.surface: Hanging bunting at the front of the cricket pavilion with a greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flags' suggests bunting; it means flagstones.
explanation.definitionFit: To pave is to lay flagstones or other slabs over ground.

clue.text: Clement. nearly six-week period keeping Spain cool to the north

indicators.note: holding something inside, so the other letters go within it

parts.note: Lent lasts forty days, nearly the forty-two of six weeks

indicators.note: in this down entry the trendy word is split around Spain, one letter of it sitting to the north

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool
E is Spain's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: A period of Lent with a mild spell over Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog reads 'to the north' as a reversal, but the letters come out right with Spain simply inside cool; the phrase is best read as positioning in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement means merciful, inclined to mildness, which is what lenient means.

clue.text: Newspaper accounts about Switzerland showing social mobility

parts.note: a rag is a low-grade newspaper

indicators.note: the accounts go around the other letters

parts.note: stories are accounts
CH is Switzerland's vehicle code

explanation.surface: Press reports about Swiss society showing class movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Rags to riches describes rising from poverty to wealth, the upward kind of class movement.

clue.text: Sellers turned up, ringing hotel for a drink

indicators.note: encircling, so the hotel goes inside
in a down clue, read upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: reps are sales representatives
the Ritz is a famous London hotel

explanation.surface: Salespeople arrive and phone a hotel bar for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A spritzer is white wine mixed with soda water, served as a long cocktail.

clue.text: Dubious sight is seen dubiously

indicators.note: in a questionable fashion, so these letters are arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A doubtful sighting, reported doubtfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie, the Loch Ness Monster, is a creature whose reported sightings are widely doubted.

clue.text: Superior sticks given a twirl

indicators.note: spinning the word round means its letters are read backwards

parts.note: gums means sticks, as with glue

explanation.surface: Someone haughty twirling their walking sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: A superior air is a self-satisfied, condescending one, so the adjective is a synonym for complacent pride.

clue.text: They may conduct endless tour behind same ground

indicators.note: in a down clue the tour comes below, after, the other piece
milled into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
the end of the word is dropped

parts.note: a trip is a tour

explanation.surface: An endless tour over the same old ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conduct' suggests guides; it means directing orchestras.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri are distinguished conductors, the Italian plural of maestro.

clue.text: Trait of sheep up north, I suspect, in Greenock's borders

indicators.note: places one set of letters inside the other
the borders of the name are its first and last letters

parts.note: G and K, the first and last letters of Greenock

indicators.note: dubious, so these letters are arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Sheep in the north of Scotland, around Greenock, behaving as a flock.
explanation.walkthrough: Greenock is a town on the Clyde in Scotland; its outer letters are G and K.
explanation.definitionFit: Groupthink is uncritical conformity to a group's opinions, the human version of flocking behaviour.

clue.text: Provider of fruit lacking taste for tart

parts.note: a vine provides grapes
garish means gaudy, showing no taste

explanation.surface: A fruit grower without refinement is fit only for a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like the pastry fed by the fruit, but it is the adjective meaning sharp or sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegarish describes a sour, acidic flavour, which is the adjective sense of tart.

clue.text: Note doctor put next to case of medicine

indicators.note: says the doctor is placed alongside the other piece, here after it
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A GP writes a note beside a box of pills.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is a short written note or memorandum.

clue.text: Poet flipping put out, eating dry rolls for convenience

indicators.note: taking in, so the letters go within
turned over, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: T S Eliot, the poet
to issue is to put out, publish
TT, teetotal, means dry

explanation.surface: A poet furiously publishing, while munching dry bread rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convenience' is the British word for a public lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilet tissue comes in rolls and is used in the lavatory, a convenience in British usage.

clue.text: Place to park behind Sierra and take in fuel

indicators.note: says the eating comes after the S

parts.note: Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to eat is to take in food, the body's fuel

explanation.surface: Finding a parking space behind a Ford Sierra and filling up the tank.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sierra was a Ford car, which suits the parking picture; here it is just the letter S. 'Park' is the slang sense: sit yourself down.
explanation.definitionFit: To park yourself is to sit down, so a chair or seat is a place to do it.

clue.text: Broadcast on pitch, not without intro from Clare Balding

indicators.note: scattered like seed, so the letters are spread into a new order
the named letter is left out of the shuffled pool
the introduction of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Clare

explanation.surface: The sports presenter Clare Balding on air from the pitch, but not quite introducing it.
explanation.walkthrough: Clare Balding is a BBC sports presenter, so 'Balding' reads as her surname. Shuffle ONPITCHNOT with the C of Clare removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thin on top has hair receding from the crown, an idiom for going bald.

clue.text: Apple could produce this stinging sensation, having high acidity

parts.note: a smart is a sharp stinging pain
pH one, read as PH ONE, is very strongly acidic

explanation.surface: An apple so sour it stings the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple' is the fruit in the picture but the tech company in the definition. A pH of one is highly acidic.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple's iPhone is a smartphone, so the company makes one.

clue.text: Army supplies ally that is infiltrating sides

parts.note: a mate is a friend or ally

indicators.note: getting inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: R and L, right and left sides
IE, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A friendly agent creeps through the flanks of the military supply lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Materiel is the equipment and stores of an armed force, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Singer drunkenly speaking made-up lingo

indicators.note: a drunk slurs S into SH, so the name said that way gives the answer

parts.note: Elvis Presley, the singer

explanation.surface: A tipsy vocalist babbling nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Slurring the S of Elvis gives the SH ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvish is the invented elf language Tolkien created for his fiction.

clue.text: Sweet poorly coated in fake rock

indicators.note: covered by, so the other piece wraps around it

parts.note: paste is glass used for imitation gems
ill means poorly

explanation.surface: A cheap candy coated in imitation stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests the seaside stick of candy; it is a gem, rock being slang for a diamond.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small chewy confection, often fruit-flavoured.

clue.text: Black out, perhaps, on the left turn

parts.note: red is the colour of the political left
an act is a turn on stage

explanation.surface: Fainting, maybe, while making a left turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black out' suggests fainting; here it is blacking out text, one way to edit for publication.
explanation.definitionFit: To redact is to edit a document, often by obscuring sensitive lines in black ink.

clue.text: Making a career — getting home with €1,000

parts.note: the punctuation mark in the clue is a dash
in means at home
G, a grand, is a thousand

explanation.surface: Building a working life by earning a thousand euros and going home.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash in the clue is itself the first piece. 'Career' is the verb: to rush headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along at speed, as is dashing.

clue.text: Chap without singular fuss getting antiquated browser

indicators.note: in the old sense outside, so the chap wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a man is a chap
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a to-do is a fuss

explanation.surface: A man not making a single fuss over his outdated web browser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browser' suggests software; it is an animal that browses on leaves, and an extinct one.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastodon was a prehistoric elephant relative that fed by browsing on shrubs and trees.

clue.text: A nude cavorting around taking too many drugs shows some guts

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the other piece
prancing about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: OD is an overdose

explanation.surface: A naked reveller high on drugs displays plenty of nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guts' suggests courage; it is the bowel.
explanation.definitionFit: The duodena are the first sections of the small intestine, so parts of the guts.

clue.text: Cash regularly securing e.g., leopard-skin carpets

indicators.note: holding, so the letters close round the other piece
taking every other letter

parts.note: C and S, alternate letters of Cash
a leopard's skin is an example of a hide

explanation.surface: Money buys a leopard-skin rug for the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpets' looks like floor coverings; it is the verb meaning reprimands.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British slang for rebuking them, the same as chiding.

clue.text: Secretaries talk about covering for delegate in spring

indicators.note: the pieces go around the other letters

parts.note: PAs are personal assistants
chat is talk

indicators.note: the covering of a word is its outer letters

explanation.surface: Office assistants gossip about standing in for a delegate during the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season; it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A pas de chat is a ballet jump, a cat-like leap, so a kind of spring.

clue.text: Player of music in international school

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: A musician at an international school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' suggests pupils; it is a group of sea mammals.
explanation.definitionFit: The iPod is Apple's portable device for playing digital music files.

clue.text: Complaint of The Observer or Vogue, cutting line

indicators.note: removing, so the line is taken out

parts.note: vogue means style, fashion

explanation.surface: A grievance from one newspaper or magazine, cutting a line of copy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer and Vogue look like publications; the observer is an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a complaint of the organ that observes.

clue.text: Fail in Cambridge University after lowest possible score?

indicators.note: says the university comes after the score

parts.note: O, nil, is the lowest score
MIT is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A student failing at Cambridge after scoring zero.
explanation.walkthrough: It is not the English Cambridge but Cambridge, Massachusetts, home of MIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit is to fail to do or include something, a verb synonym.

clue.text: A grant: small bit of cash for a developer still

parts.note: the dole is a state payment
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: A grant offering only a little money to a property developer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developer' suggests property; here it is a person still growing up.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is still maturing physically, so an adolescent is someone still developing.

clue.text: So Oscar goes after some work

parts.note: an erg is a unit of work in physics
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: So Oscar is off after a bit of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, used as a conjunction like so.

clue.text: Fool judge, swallowing first lawbreaker's claim

indicators.note: taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to rate is to judge
Eve broke God's first command in Eden

explanation.surface: A judge fooled by a criminal's statement.
explanation.definitionFit: To asseverate is to declare or assert solemnly, a formal synonym.
